properties.description: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind (2004), directed by Michel Gondry and written by Charlie Kaufman, is a drama-romance with speculative science fiction elements starring Jim Carrey and Kate Winslet, with Tom Wilkinson and Mark Ruffalo in supporting roles. The story follows a man who undergoes a medical procedure to erase memories of his ex and then fights to preserve moments of their relationship as they are deleted. Combining nonlinear, dreamlike sequences with raw emotional scenes, the film explores themes of memory, identity, regret, and the paradoxes of love. Its tone is melancholic and thought‑provoking, balancing surreal visual inventiveness with intimate character work.
properties.plot_summary: After their relationship collapses, a couple turn to an experimental clinic that can erase specific memories of a person from one’s mind. As the procedure progresses, the man relives their time together inside his own consciousness and begins to resist the deletions. His attempts to hide and preserve precious moments force him to confront the full complexity of their love, heartbreak, and the role of memory in identity. The film interweaves surreal, dreamlike sequences with intimate, emotionally raw scenes to explore whether erasing pain also erases what made life meaningful.

properties.description: Her (2013), directed by Spike Jonze and starring Joaquin Phoenix, Amy Adams, and Scarlett Johansson, is a near‑future romantic drama that follows a lonely writer who forms a deep bond with an advanced operating system. The film blends melancholic character study and speculative science fiction to explore loneliness, identity, and the ethics of emotional dependence on technology. Warm visuals, restrained performances, and a bittersweet tone make it a reflective meditation on intimacy in a digitally mediated age.
properties.plot_summary: In a near‑future, tech‑saturated city, a lonely writer who composes intimate letters for others adopts a newly released operating system with a distinctly human voice. As the OS learns and grows, their relationship deepens from companionship into romance, forcing both to confront attachment, identity, and what it means to be present. The story traces the emotional consequences of leaning on artificial intimacy while exploring grief, longing, and the porous boundary between human and machine.

properties.description: Trainspotting (1996), directed by Danny Boyle and adapted from Irvine Welsh's novel, stars Ewan McGregor alongside a supporting ensemble including Ewen Bremner, Jonny Lee Miller, Robert Carlyle, and Kelly Macdonald. The film is a raw, often darkly comic drama about a young man's attempts to break free from heroin addiction and the complex loyalties of his friends in Edinburgh. Combining surreal visual flourishes with social realism, it interrogates addiction, poverty, and the possibility of personal redemption while maintaining a sharply ironic voice.
properties.plot_summary: Set in Edinburgh, a young man deeply embedded in the local heroin scene tries to quit and rebuild his life while constantly pulled back by addiction and the influence of his circle. The film follows his uneasy attempts at detox, fleeting moments of hope, and the betrayals and loyalties that define his friendships. Surreal, darkly comic sequences are interwoven with gritty realism to portray the physical and emotional toll of substance dependence.

properties.description: Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance) (2014), directed by Alejandro G. Iñárritu, is a darkly comic drama starring Michael Keaton, Edward Norton and Zach Galifianakis. The film follows a former superhero movie star who writes, directs and stars in a Broadway play as he confronts fame, ego, and a destabilizing inner voice. Stylistically notable for its long-take illusion, jazz-driven rhythm and backstage setting, the movie explores themes of artistic integrity, identity, and the porous line between reality and performance while mixing satire with psychological intensity.
properties.plot_summary: A once-famous movie star best known for playing a superhero struggles to reclaim relevance by writing, directing, and starring in a new Broadway play. As opening night approaches he battles crippling self-doubt, public scrutiny, and a powerful inner voice that manifests as his former on-screen persona. The production’s tense backstage world exposes rivalries, fragile relationships, and the blurring of performance and reality. The film moves between darkly comic satire and surreal psychological episodes as the protagonist pursues artistic validation at great personal cost.

properties.description: Donnie Darko (2001), written and directed by Richard Kelly and starring Jake Gyllenhaal, Jena Malone and Mary McDonnell, is a moody, genre-blending drama/psychological sci‑fi thriller. The film follows a troubled teenager who, after narrowly avoiding a bizarre accident, is visited by visions of a man in a rabbit suit that set him on a path of strange, morally fraught actions. Mixing adolescent coming-of-age elements with time-travel paradoxes, the story examines mental illness, fate, and the porous line between reality and delusion. Its tone is haunting, melancholic, and provocatively ambiguous, which has cemented the film's cult status.
properties.plot_summary: After narrowly escaping a bizarre accident, a troubled teenager begins experiencing vivid, often terrifying visions of a man in a large rabbit suit who instructs and manipulates him. As the visions intensify he skips medication, clashes with authority figures, and becomes obsessed with understanding the nature of his reality. Strange events and hints of time manipulation draw him toward a series of morally fraught actions that force him to confront fate, mortality, and his own mental state.
